requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Marking.** `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` (md/requirements/cli.md) anchors `:impl: assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. That is the only impl site, and it is the complete skill file. A skill is prose, so an anchor is the intended way to mark it (see the "Some sources cannot or should not carry a reference themselves" passage in md/reference.md and `requirements.references.anchors`).

**The skill meets each obligation in the requirement.**
- **Bundled.** `Cargo.toml` declares `[[package.metadata.symposium.skills]] source.path = "assets/skills"`, so the skill ships with the crate. `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py` is tagged `{test}` for `requirements.integration.symposium`. It checks that every directory under `assets/skills` with a `SKILL.md` is installed byte-identical and refreshed on a version change, so it covers this skill too.
- **Read code and tests.** The opening paragraph says to read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation and tests. It adds that agents should follow behavior through the code rather than relying only on test names or top-level dispatch.
- **Map every first-party test.**
  - The first working inventory covers every runnable test or case, including integration tests, doctests and parameterized cases, with the requirement or example IDs each checks.
  - The skill requires at least one `{test}` reference with a full name on each test definition or case. It forbids a file-level tag standing in for unrelated tests.
- **Map every source unit implementing end-user-visible behavior.**
  - The second inventory covers every explicit function or method, including trait declarations and helpers, plus public APIs, commands, handlers, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches.
  - Each function needs an `{impl}` reference where it implements part of a definition. A reference on an enclosing module or `impl` does not cover its functions.
  - A tagged entry point is not accepted as coverage for deeper code.
  - An unclear user-facing candidate stays on the gap list.
  - Internal-detail requirements may not justify end-user-visible behavior.
- **Report gaps, not unreviewed completeness.** The closing paragraph requires independent review of both inventories against source and tests before claiming complete coverage. It requires reporting mapped counts over total counts and claiming 100% only when nothing is unmapped and every observable branch is reviewed. It requires listing remaining gaps with locations and reasons, and forbids silent exclusions.

**Extra behavior.** The skill also covers user agreement on proposed requirements, `habeas author --all`, and the "no hand-written evidence" rule. Other requirements mark this same file as `{impl}` and specify those points: `requirements_review_skill`, `behavior_review_guidance`, `internal_detail_guidance` and `authoring.batch`. So I found no unspecified behavior.

**Tests.** There is no test of the skill's text. For a natural-language guidance file I think that is justifiable, because a string-match test would be brittle and would not show that the guidance is adequate. The requirement's evidence review reads the file in full, and the smoke test above verifies bundling and installation. I found no gaps and no FIXMEs.
